neighbours.label: The preposition "in" when a law, statute, code, decree or official rule is said to be still in something, i.e. right where "in force / in effect / in use" is coming (also German "noch in"); weaker after "remained". Silent for "in" after subjects that are not rules (people, buildings, objects) and for rules with other prepositions or verbs (under review, entered into, came into). Not claimed: its strongest top examples, mid-word pieces of names (Bon-aparte, Geschäfts-f-ührung).
